route: The drive line of a driven block: the orientations a block presents along its drive, what a doubling translate costs on it, and the escape shape at the third level
object: THE DRIVE LINE of a driven block (def:pinned): the step function t |-> s_B(t) from the drive [0,1] to the improvement outmaps of the m-cube, read as a WALK IN THE COMBED-FLIP GRAPH of unique sink orientations -- the graph whose edges reverse one edge of the cube whose two endpoints have the same bottom-antipodal successor -- together with the ESCAPE EXTENSION of def:pinned in which the rest actions of the outer pair also read the block, whose whole outmap turns out to be carried by three drive functions w00, w10, w01 and one comparison rho.
headline: A drive line is a walk in the combed-flip graph: at a simple fence exactly one edge reverses, and an edge of a USO may be reversed alone iff its two endpoints have the SAME bottom-antipodal successor (then the flip transposes the outmap and reverses its sign) -- the level-two block's drive line has 14 cells and 13 fences, all simple, and passes from B^1 to B^1(.xor e_beta1) in exactly 8 fences = the flip distance, a geodesic; d(B^2, B^2(.xor z)) = 42, 52, 32, 44 for the four doubling z = 8,10,24,26, with no monotone combed AUSO path at all for z = 24, 26. For the escape shape of rem:pinned-escape I prove a level theorem (three drives and one comparison reproduce the whole outmap; verified exactly against both published realisations, prop:b2-realised and prop:b3-outer) and, from the consistency of the three drive comparisons, that NO escape extension of ANY block realises a translate with a nonzero beta-component -- killing z = 24 and 26 outright; over the level-two block z = 10 is killed by the drive line itself and z = 8 unless R_alpha - C_alpha is mixed in sign, which is the one case left open.

results.name: dl:flippable -- a single edge of a unique sink orientation may be reversed iff its endpoints share their bottom-antipodal successor
results.statement: Let s be a unique sink orientation of the m-cube, e = {sigma, sigma xor e_v} an edge and s^e the orientation obtained by reversing e alone. (a) s^e is a unique sink orientation iff s(sigma) xor s(sigma xor e_v) = {v}, equivalently iff sigma xor s(sigma) = (sigma xor e_v) xor s(sigma xor e_v): the two endpoints have the same bottom-antipodal successor. Call such an edge COMBED. Reversing a combed edge EXCHANGES the outmap values of its endpoints, so (the outmap of a USO being a bijection of {0,1}^m) s^e = s composed with a transposition and sgn(s) is reversed. (b) If s is acyclic and e is combed, oriented sigma -> sigma', then s^e is acyclic iff s has no directed sigma -> sigma' path other than e. (c) Writing d(s,s') for the number of edges the two orient differently and D(s,s') for the least number of combed flips through USOs, D >= d and D = d mod 2; and since translation by z != 0 is an even permutation for m >= 2, sgn(s(. xor z)) = sgn(s), so reachability of s(. xor z) from s forces d(s, s(. xor z)) to be even.
results.why_not_implied: lem:crossing is a law about 2-faces of the improvement orientation of a GAME (when g_i can be non-constant on a square, and what that forbids for affine separation); it says nothing about modifying an abstract orientation, and in particular nothing about when reversing a single edge leaves a unique sink orientation, which is a condition on 1-faces and their containing faces and is proved here from the Szabo-Welzl condition alone.
results.argument: (a) Faces omitting the direction v are untouched. For J containing v and F the face through sigma with directions J, write A = s(sigma), B = s(sigma') with v in A, v not in B. After the flip sigma' is never a sink of F, sigma is one iff A cap J = {v}, and the other vertices are unchanged; before the flip sigma is not a sink and sigma' is one iff B cap J = empty. So F keeps exactly one sink iff [A cap J = {v}] <=> [B cap J = empty] for every J containing v; taking J = {v,w} gives A minus {v} = B, and that condition makes the equivalence hold for every J. Injectivity of the outmap is the Szabo-Welzl condition. (b) s being acyclic, a cycle of s^e must use e, i.e. contain a directed sigma -> sigma' path of s avoiding e. (c) Each flip changes exactly one edge, so the parity of the number of flips at each edge decides whether it differs; the sign statement is (a) plus sgn(T_z) = (-1)^{2^{m-1}} = +1.
results.verification: EXHAUSTIVE at m = 2 and m = 3: all 12 and all 744 unique sink orientations, all 48 and all 8928 single-edge flips, 0 violations of the law. SAMPLED at m = 3,4,5,6: 200/120/40/12 random USOs (generated by random combed-flip walks from the identity outmap), 2400/3840/3200/2304 flips, 0 violations; the acyclicity law of (b) tested on 1155/1395/524/139 combed flips of acyclic USOs, 0 violations (dl_verify_flip.py, flip_laws_check.txt). The parity consequence of (c) was checked against reality: over all 66 and all 276396 pairs of USOs of the 2- and 3-cubes, d(s,s') = [sgn s != sgn s'] mod 2 without exception, and for B^2 against all 31 of its translates sgn = +1 throughout and every d is even -- so the sign is a genuine invariant of the flip but yields no obstruction (recorded as dl:sign).

results.name: dl:drive-flip -- a drive line moves by single combed flips, so its fences are bounded below by a flip distance
results.statement: Let B be a driven block and t_0 a drive at which exactly one edge e of the m-cube ties, the block being nondegenerate on a punctured neighbourhood of t_0 (a SIMPLE fence). Then s_B(t_0^-) and s_B(t_0^+) agree off e; if they differ, e is combed in both and satisfies dl:flippable(b) in each. Consequently, for t < t' at which the block is nondegenerate, if every fence in (t,t') is simple then their number is at least the combed-flip distance D(s_B(t), s_B(t')), hence at least the edge-flip distance d.
results.why_not_implied: rem:pinned-escape prints two exact fences of one drive line and asks whether a non-pinned block can present B^2 and a doubling translate at two drives; it contains no statement about what happens AT a fence, no notion of a combed edge, and therefore no lower bound on the number of fences separating two presented orientations.
results.argument: Every margin other than the two of e is nonzero at t_0 and continuous in t (val_sigma(t) is a componentwise minimum of finitely many affine maps, by thm:stopping-determinacy applied to the frozen block), hence of constant sign near t_0; so only e can reverse. Both one-sided limits are improvement outmaps of nondegenerate stopping games, hence acyclic unique sink orientations (prop:allsw-auso), and they differ in one edge, so dl:flippable applies. A sequence of simple fences is therefore a combed-flip path.
results.verification: Verified on the level-two block of prop:b2-realised driven by y_{c5}: its drive line has 13 fences, EVERY one simple, and at every one the tied set is exactly the predicted pair of incidences {(sigma,v),(sigma xor e_v, v)}, the two value vectors agree exactly, the outmap changes in exactly one edge, and that edge is combed in the orientation on the left (dl_fences.py, fences_check.txt; 13/13, no exception, exact rational arithmetic).

results.name: dl:fences -- how many fences a drive line can have and how big they are
results.statement: Let B be a driven block with n = m+k controlled vertices whose rows are dyadic of denominator 2^D and leak. (a) each incidence changes sign at most 2^k times, and the drive line has at most 2^m((m+1)2^k - 1) < (m+1)2^{m+k} fences; (b) for k = 0 each margin is affine, each edge reverses at most once, no orientation recurs, and there are at most m 2^{m-1} fences; (c) EVERY FENCE IS A RATIONAL p/q WITH 0 < q <= 2^{(n+1)(D+1)} AND |p| <= q.
results.why_not_implied: rem:b2-anatomy reports the frozen block's outmap at a few drives measured on a grid and records two fence values; it gives no count of fences, no dependence on m and k, and above all no arithmetic bound on a fence -- (c) is a statement about the denominators of the drive at which a game degenerates, which nothing in the paper addresses.
results.argument: (a),(b): freezing at (sigma,tau) gives (I-P)x = q + r t with (I-P)^{-1} >= 0 and r >= 0, so each profile value is affine and nondecreasing in t, and val_sigma is their componentwise minimum, hence concave piecewise affine with at most 2^k pieces (each tau-optimality region is an intersection of half-lines, hence an interval, and they cover [0,1]); on each piece each of the m margins is affine and vanishes at most once; ties come in edge pairs (lem:flat-class), which halves the count when k = 0. (c) On a tau-cell the pair (x,t) at which the incidence (sigma,v) ties solves the (n+1)x(n+1) system (I-P)x - r t = q, (p^{v,1-sigma_v} - e_v).x + r^{v,1-sigma_v} t = -q^{v,1-sigma_v}; multiplied by 2^D the matrix is integral with every row of l1 norm at most 2^{D+1}, so Cramer plus Hadamard gives t as a quotient of integers bounded by 2^{(D+1)(n+1)}.
results.verification: On the level-two block (m=3, k=1, n=4, D=9) the bound (a) gives 64 and the true count is 13; the bound (c) gives 2^{50} = 1.126e15 and the largest numerator or denominator among the 13 exact fences is 48259671705 = 4.83e10 (dl_final_check.py, final_check.txt). HONESTY NOTE: parts (a) and (b) reprove, in a slightly sharper per-sigma form, the round-17 realisation-space route's rs:drive(b),(c),(d), which was NOT integrated into frontier.tex; the new content of this result is (c) and the (m+1)2^{m+k} form of the count.

results.name: dl:b2-line -- the level-two block's drive line in full, and the realised doubling as a geodesic
results.statement: The level-two block {c1,c2,c3,c6} of prop:b2-realised driven by y_{c5} has a drive line with exactly 14 maximal cells and 13 fences on [0,1]; every fence is simple and the reversed edge is combed in the orientation on its left. The cells are, in order, (0,1,3,6,7,4,5,2) = B^1, (0,1,3,6,5,4,7,2), (0,1,3,2,5,4,7,6), (1,0,3,2,5,4,7,6), (5,0,3,2,1,4,7,6), (5,4,3,2,1,0,7,6), (5,4,7,2,1,0,3,6), (5,4,7,2,0,1,3,6), (7,4,5,2,0,1,3,6) = B^1(. xor e_beta1), (7,4,5,6,0,1,3,2), (7,6,5,4,0,1,3,2), (7,6,5,4,0,1,2,3), (7,6,4,5,0,1,2,3), (7,6,4,5,0,3,2,1). Since d(B^1, B^1(. xor e_beta1)) = 8 and the block passes from the one to the other in exactly 8 fences, its drive line is a GEODESIC of the combed-flip graph: the one doubling that is realised costs the least number of fences dl:drive-flip allows.
results.why_not_implied: rem:pinned-escape gives the two windows of that drive line on which the block has outmap B^1 and its translate (three of the thirteen fences); it does not give the other eleven fences, the twelve intermediate orientations, the fact that every fence is simple, nor -- since it has no notion of flip distance -- that the passage is a geodesic.
results.argument: The cells are computed by collecting all roots of all profile-value crossings and all margins on all tau-cells, sorting them and evaluating the outmap at the midpoints in exact arithmetic; simplicity and combedness at each fence are then checked directly, and the geodesic statement is dl:drive-flip together with the computed d = 8.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic throughout (dl_line.py, dl_fences.py; outputs in fences_check.txt and driveline.json). The 13 fences are 47723619/255897160, 6856791/18130160, 23232377303/48259671705, 1368077078/2659981905, 3079758983/5976346345, 4449774213/8325926890, 747670031/1324418625, 1175936917/2026652880, 10168377/16341335, 315968817/435909343, 1070103399/1278421945, 16114985061/18836958955, 2267378637/2318632595; the first, eighth and ninth are the three printed in rem:pinned-escape, so this reproduces them and adds ten. At each fence the tied incidences are exactly one edge pair, the two value vectors coincide exactly, and the reversed edge lies in the combed set of the left orientation (13/13). An independent monotone combed-flip search finds a path B^1 -> B^1(. xor 4) of length 8 through acyclic USOs (dl_bfs.py).

results.name: dl:b2-distance -- the four doubling translations at the second level, and what no counting can give
results.statement: B^2 has exactly 17 combed edges among its 80, and d(B^2, B^2(. xor z)) = 42, 52, 32, 44 for z = 8, 10, 24, 26, the four doubling translations of cor:pinned-no-doubling. In the combed-flip graph restricted to ACYCLIC unique sink orientations there is a distance-decreasing path of length 42 from B^2 to B^2(. xor 8) -- so the combed-flip distance there is exactly 42 -- and NO path of length at most d+4 to B^2(. xor 24) or to B^2(. xor 26), so D(B^2, B^2(. xor 24)) >= 38 and D(B^2, B^2(. xor 26)) >= 50. Hence a drive line joining B^2 to either of those two through simple fences needs strictly more fences than the flip distance. WHAT DOES NOT FOLLOW: by dl:fences(a) a block with m = 5 Max and k Min vertices has room for (m+1)2^{m+k} = 192*2^k fences while the flip distance never exceeds m 2^{m-1} = 80, so no lower bound on (m,k,D) follows from counting fences at any k; the fence count is not the invariant that measures the cost of a level.
results.why_not_implied: cor:pinned-no-doubling excludes the doubly pinned shape from realising B_phi(B^2,z) for those four z by an up-closedness argument at the outer pair and computes the shape's height cap 16; it contains no metric on orientations, no flip distance, and no statement about how many degeneracies a family of games interpolating between two orientations must pass through.
results.argument: The distances are direct counts. The reachability statements are exhaustive depth-first searches of the subgraph of combed flips that (i) reduce the flip distance to the target at every step, or (ii) allow at most one or two distance-increasing flips, with memoisation, requiring acyclicity at every intermediate; a path of length d + 2j uses exactly j increasing flips, so 'no path with at most 2 increasing flips' means D >= d + 6.
results.verification: dl_bfs.py and dl_bfs2.py, exact integer arithmetic on outmaps. z = 8: monotone path of length 42 found (10753 nodes). z = 24 (d = 32): none with 0, 1 or 2 increasing flips (1620, 69761, 1418276 nodes, searches completed, budget 1.5e6). z = 26 (d = 44): none with 0, 1 or 2 (81, 19777, 841073 nodes, completed). Dropping the acyclicity requirement (USOs only) still gives none with 0 or 1 increasing flips for either (4357/183291 and 129/35869 nodes). z = 10: the monotone search was cut short at 300001 nodes and is reported as undecided. Combed-edge counts and sgn(B^2) = +1 from dl_final_check.py.

results.name: dl:escape-level -- the level theorem for the escape shape: three drives and one comparison
results.statement: Call ESCAPE EXTENSION of a driven block B with drive beta the game on C u {alpha,beta}, alpha,beta in Vmax, with alpha: (0) A y_beta + C_alpha.y + q_A, (1) R_alpha.y + q'_A and beta: (0) A' y_alpha + C_beta.y + q_B, (1) R_beta.y + q'_B, all rows substochastic with a strict leak and no block row reading alpha (def:pinned is C_alpha = C_beta = 0). Put Delta = 1-AA', Dhat = (A'C_alpha + C_beta)/Delta, ehat = (A'q_A + q_B)/Delta, D_1 = A'R_alpha + C_beta, e_1 = A'q'_A + q_B, and let Phi_sigma(c,d) be the unique t in [0,1] with t = c.y_sigma(t) + d. Then with w00 = Phi_sigma(Dhat,ehat), w10 = Phi_sigma(D_1,e_1), w01 = Phi_sigma(R_beta,q'_B) and rho(sigma,t) = (R_alpha - C_alpha).y_sigma(t) + (q'_A - q_A) - A t: the drive at the inner strategy sigma is w00, w10, w01, w01 on the layers (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1); the INNER part of the outmap at (sigma,L) is s_B(w_L(sigma))(sigma), a pointwise selection from the drive line rather than one frozen orientation; and the OUTER part is given by the four bits P = [w00<w10], Q = [w00<w01], R = [w10<w01], S = [rho(sigma,w01)>0] through O_(0,0) = (P,Q), O_(1,0) = (1-P,R), O_(0,1) = (S,1-Q), O_(1,1) = (1-S,1-R). In particular alpha's switchability on (0,0) and (1,0) is complementary, and so is beta's on (0,0)/(0,1) and on (1,0)/(1,1).
results.why_not_implied: prop:pinned-level states conditions (C1)-(C5) for the PINNED shape, in which the layer-(0,0) values are the two constants Theta_u, Theta_w; it does not cover a rest action that reads the block, it has no drive functions w00, w10, w01 -- with C_alpha = C_beta = 0 the first is a constant and the other two are not formed at all -- and its (C5) is 'the block frozen at the layer's drive has outmap s', which is false in the escape shape, where the drive depends on the inner strategy and the inner part is a diagonal selection.
results.argument: Freezing the outer pair at a layer leaves a 2x2 system in (y_alpha,y_beta) whose block input is y_sigma(y_beta) (lem:readout: no block row reads alpha). At (0,0) elimination gives y_beta(1-AA') = (A'C_alpha+C_beta).y + A'q_A + q_B, i.e. y_beta = Dhat.y + ehat; at (1,0), y_beta = A'(R_alpha y + q'_A) + C_beta y + q_B = D_1.y + e_1; at (0,1) and (1,1), y_beta = R_beta y + q'_B, the same on both. Each fixed point is unique because the map is nondecreasing with slope |c|_1 sup||y'_sigma||_inf < 1, using y'_sigma = (I-P)^{-1} r <= (I-P)^{-1}(1 - P.1) = 1. For the outer bits: 'alpha switchable at (0,0)' is R_alpha y + q'_A > y_alpha; multiplying by A' > 0 and adding C_beta y + q_B turns it into D_1.y + e_1 > w00, i.e. w00 < w10. 'alpha switchable at (1,0)' is A w10 + C_alpha y + q_A > R_alpha y + q'_A; the same manipulation gives Delta(Dhat.y + ehat) > Delta w10, i.e. w10 < w00. 'beta switchable at (0,0)' resp. (1,0) is R_beta y + q'_B > w00 resp. > w10; at (0,1) it is A'(A w01 + C_alpha y + q_A) + C_beta y + q_B > w01, i.e. w00 > w01; at (1,1) it is D_1.y + e_1 > w01, i.e. w10 > w01. Finally alpha at (0,1)/(1,1) compares R_alpha y + q'_A with A w01 + C_alpha y + q_A, whose difference is rho(sigma,w01).
results.verification: Checked exactly against BOTH published realisations, from their printed normal forms. (i) prop:b2-realised (138 vertices, block {c1,c2,c3,c6}, pin (502,509,8,0)/512): the theorem returns Theta_w = ehat = 2036/3313 and Theta_u = 2048/3313, exactly the paper's numbers, and the four bits plus the diagonal inner reading reproduce the WHOLE outmap B^2 -- all 8 inner strategies, all 4 layers, outer and inner parts -- with no mismatch (dl_verify_b2.py, b2_level_check.txt). (ii) prop:b3-outer (194 vertices, block = the level-two game itself, 5 Max and 1 Min, undriven, pin (1021,1023,2,0)/1024): the theorem returns Theta_u = 2048/4093 (the paper's value) and Theta_w = 2046/4093 and reproduces the outer part of B_p(B^2,0) at all 32 inner strategies with no mismatch (dl_verify_b3.py, b3_level_check.txt).

results.name: dl:tournament and dl:no-beta-translate -- no escape extension translates by its beta-coordinate
results.statement: (dl:tournament) In a nondegenerate stopping escape extension the three bits P = [w00<w10], Q = [w00<w01], R = [w10<w01] of dl:escape-level are, at every inner strategy, the pairwise comparisons of three real numbers, so (P,Q,R) is never (1,0,1) or (0,1,0). (dl:no-beta-translate) Consequently, if zeta = (w, zeta_alpha, zeta_beta) has zeta_beta = 1 and the readout phi takes the value 0 somewhere -- which the parity of the bottom-antipodal height always does, at the sink -- then B_phi(s,z')(. xor zeta) is the improvement outmap of NO nondegenerate stopping escape extension with outer pair (alpha,beta): not for any A, A', any readouts C_alpha, C_beta, R_alpha, R_beta, any constants, and ANY BLOCK. In particular, of the four doubling translations z in {8,10,24,26} of cor:pinned-no-doubling, the two carrying the beta_2 bit, z = 24 and z = 26, are dead for the escape shape as well as for the pinned one.
results.why_not_implied: thm:pinned-no-translate excludes every translate with a nonzero outer component for the PINNED shape, by an up-closedness argument that uses the constancy of the layer-(0,0) outer values; rem:pinned-escape names exactly the shape in which that constancy is lost and states that the lemma 'then says nothing'. The present theorem covers that shape, and its mechanism is different: not monotonicity but the transitivity of the order on three drives, which the pinned proof never forms.
results.argument: Read the outer part of the target at the layer L off the table of thm:blowup at the layer L xor (zeta_alpha,zeta_beta), and write phitilde(sigma) = phi(sigma xor w). For (zeta_alpha,zeta_beta) = (0,1) one gets P = [phitilde = 1], Q = 1, R = [phitilde = 1], which at a sigma with phitilde(sigma) = 0 is (0,1,0): w10 < w00 < w01 < w10. For (1,1) one gets P = [phitilde = 0], Q = [phitilde = 1], R = 1, which at the same sigma is (1,0,1): w00 < w10 < w01 while w01 < w00. Both are cycles among three reals.
results.verification: The four complementarity laws of dl:escape-level, on which the tournament rests, are validated exactly on prop:b2-realised (8 strategies x 4 layers, no mismatch) and prop:b3-outer (32 strategies, no mismatch). Independently, the blow-up table itself satisfies all four complementarities at every layer and both parities -- a nontrivial consistency check that the shape is exactly right for the untranslated blow-up. The exclusion is consistent with the flip-distance evidence: z = 24 and 26 are precisely the two translations for which no monotone combed path to B^2 exists (dl:b2-distance).

results.name: dl:escape-mixed, dl:escape-updown and dl:m3-decision -- the decision at m = 3 over the level-two block
results.statement: Let G be a nondegenerate stopping escape extension whose outmap is B_phi(s,z')(. xor zeta) with zeta_alpha = 1, zeta_beta = 0, and suppose phitilde takes the value 1 somewhere. (dl:escape-mixed) Then R_alpha - C_alpha cannot be <= 0 componentwise. (dl:escape-updown) If R_alpha - C_alpha >= 0 componentwise (the pinned shape is C_alpha = 0) then for any two inner strategies sigma, sigma' with y_sigma <= y_sigma' componentwise throughout [w01(sigma), w00(sigma')], phitilde(sigma) = 0 forces phitilde(sigma') = 0: the set {phitilde = 0} is up-closed. So either R_alpha - C_alpha is MIXED in sign or an up-closedness holds. (dl:m3-decision) Over the level-two block of prop:b2-realised with (alpha,beta) = (alpha_2,beta_2) and target B^2(. xor z): (a) z = 24 and z = 26 are excluded for every escape extension of every block by dl:no-beta-translate; (b) z = 10 is excluded over this block for a purely inner reason -- the layer (0,0) demands s_B(w00(sigma))(sigma) = B^1(sigma xor e_alpha1), which is impossible at sigma in {0,2,3,5,7} because the drive line never takes those values there, and the layer (1,0) fails likewise at sigma in {1,4,5,6}; (c) z = 8 is excluded over this block for every escape extension with R_alpha >= C_alpha, because on [0, 23232377303/48259671705] -- which contains every drive the conditions allow -- one has y_6 <= y_3 componentwise while psi(6) = 0 and psi(3) = 1, contradicting the up-closedness (seven further pairs (2,1),(2,3),(2,7),(4,1),(5,1),(6,1),(6,7) do the same).
results.why_not_implied: lem:pinned-upclosed proves up-closedness of an outer switchable set on the PINNED layer, where the outer values are constants and the switchability condition is one monotone functional against a constant; rem:pinned-escape records that in the escape shape the condition becomes a difference of two monotone functionals and that the lemma then says nothing. The statements here re-establish an up-closedness in the escape shape under an explicit sign hypothesis on R_alpha - C_alpha, and prove separately that the opposite sign is outright impossible -- a trichotomy the paper does not have, and one that identifies exactly which escape can work.
results.argument: dl:escape-mixed: if R_alpha - C_alpha <= 0 then rho(sigma,.) is strictly decreasing (y_sigma nondecreasing, minus A t); but at a phitilde-odd sigma the table demands rho(sigma,w01) < 0 with w01 < w00 and rho(sigma,w00) > 0 (the latter is P = 1), so rho must increase across [w01,w00]. dl:escape-updown: with R_alpha >= C_alpha and y_sigma concave (dl:tie), rho(sigma,.) is concave and rho(sigma,.) <= rho(sigma',.) wherever y_sigma <= y_sigma'. Suppose phitilde(sigma) = 0 and phitilde(sigma') = 1; then rho(sigma,w01(sigma)) > 0, hence rho(sigma',w01(sigma)) > 0; w01(sigma) <= w01(sigma') because R_beta >= 0; rho(sigma',w01(sigma')) < 0; and rho(sigma',w00(sigma')) > 0 with w01(sigma') < w00(sigma'). A concave function cannot be positive, negative, positive at three increasing arguments. For (b) and (c) the drive ranges are pinned down by the windows: for sigma = 3 and sigma = 6 the demands w00, w01 < w10 and w10 in the translate window force all four drives into [0, 0.37819...), where the comparison holds.
results.verification: All exact (dl_final_check.py, final_check.txt). The drive-line values taken at each sigma are {0,1,5,7}, {0,1,4,6}, {3,4,5,7}, {2,4,5,6}, {0,1,5,7}, {0,1,3,4}, {2,3,5,7}, {1,2,3,6}, which decides (b) at nine strategy-layer pairs. For (c), y_6(t) <= y_3(t) componentwise was verified at every breakpoint of both piecewise-affine curves in [0, 6856791/18130160], which proves it on the whole interval. On the wider range [0, 23232377303/48259671705] there are 8 comparable pairs (psi-even <= psi-odd) and 5 comparable pairs (psi-odd <= psi-even), so {psi = 0} is NEITHER up- nor down-closed -- which is why the block is a candidate at all and why the sign condition of dl:escape-mixed cannot be avoided. MEASURED, NOT A RESULT: an exploration over the sixteen parameters (A, A', Dhat, ehat, D_1, e_1, R_beta, q'_B) with a smooth penalty, several thousand multistart local optimisations in floats, never reached feasibility for z = 8; the best residual was 0.939 and the surviving violations always sat at the inner strategy sigma = 1, whose window [0,0.4814) for w00, w01 and window [0.5153,0.7248) for w10 are the closest together. A search is not a proof and nothing is claimed from it.

prior_art: From memory, flagged UNCHECKED against the sources. (i) The combed-edge characterisation of dl:flippable is, in the language of abstract cubes, the statement that an edge of a unique sink orientation may be reversed alone iff it is a 'combed' edge of every 2-face containing it; the notion of a combed coordinate and the reversal of edges appear in the USO literature of Szabo and Welzl and in Schurr and Szabo's work on jumping in abstract cubes, and the fact that the outmap of a USO is a bijection is Szabo-Welzl. I have not seen the flip graph of USOs under single combed reversals studied, but I cannot exclude that it is known; nothing is imported -- the characterisation is proved here from the Szabo-Welzl condition alone. (ii) That a deformed cube has one combed coordinate is used in the paper itself (the discussion after prop:km-measured), so the word is the paper's. (iii) The parametric family t -> s_B(t) is a one-parameter family of LCPs when k = 0 (through prop:oneplayer-lp and the profile LCP of thm:profile-uso), and one-parameter families of LCPs are the setting of Lemke's method (Cottle-Pang-Stone); but the parameter here moves the RIGHT-HAND SIDE through a fixed nonnegative direction while the matrix is fixed, which is the standard parametric-LCP setting, and the paper's own bias homotopy (sec:bias) is a different parametrisation, as cor:two-homotopies already records for the stopping-probability path. (iv) The determinantal fence bound is the usual Cramer-plus-Hadamard bound on the coordinates of a vertex of a rational polyhedron. (v) No theorem beyond the paper's four imported facts is used: thm:determinacy (through thm:stopping-determinacy for the frozen block), and nothing else -- Holt-Klee, Legendre and Samelson-Thrall-Wesler are not used at all in this route.

% Full paste-ready file: <code_dir>/dl_results.tex  (490 lines, environments balanced,
% labels dl:sec, dl:def, dl:tie, dl:fences, dl:flippable, dl:drive-flip, dl:b2-line,
% dl:b2-distance, dl:escsec, dl:escape, dl:escape-level, dl:tournament,
% dl:no-beta-translate, dl:updown-general, dl:escape-mixed, dl:escape-updown,
% dl:m3-decision, dl:two-sided, dl:sign).  The four central statements:

\begin{proposition}[Which single edges of a unique sink orientation can be reversed]\label{dl:flippable}
Let $s$ be an outmap of the $m$-cube, $e=\{\sigma,\sigma\oplus e_v\}$ an edge, and $s^{e}$ the
orientation obtained by reversing $e$ alone.
(a) If $s$ is a unique sink orientation, then $s^{e}$ is one if and only if
$s(\sigma)\oplus s(\sigma\oplus e_v)=\{v\}$, equivalently
$\sigma\oplus s(\sigma)=(\sigma\oplus e_v)\oplus s(\sigma\oplus e_v)$: the two endpoints of $e$
have the same bottom-antipodal successor. Call such an edge \emph{combed}. Reversing a combed
edge exchanges the outmap values of its two endpoints; since the outmap of a unique sink
orientation is a bijection of $\{0,1\}^{m}$, a combed flip composes it with a transposition and
reverses its sign as a permutation.
(b) Let $s$ be acyclic and $e$ combed, oriented $\sigma\to\sigma'$. Then $s^{e}$ is acyclic if and
only if $s$ has no directed path from $\sigma$ to $\sigma'$ other than $e$ itself.
(c) Write $d(s,s')$ for the number of edges the two orient differently and $D(s,s')$ for the least
number of combed flips carrying $s$ to $s'$ through unique sink orientations. Then $D\ge d$ and
$D\equiv d\pmod 2$; and if $s'=s(\cdot\oplus z)$ with $z\ne0$ and $m\ge2$ then
$\operatorname{sgn}s'=\operatorname{sgn}s$, so $D(s,s(\cdot\oplus z))<\infty$ forces
$d(s,s(\cdot\oplus z))$ to be even.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(a) Faces not containing the direction $v$ are untouched. Let $J\ni v$ and let $F$ be the face
through $\sigma$ with directions $J$; write $A:=s(\sigma)$, $B:=s(\sigma\oplus e_v)$, and orient
$e$ as $\sigma\to\sigma'$, so $v\in A$, $v\notin B$. After the flip $\sigma'$ is never a sink of
$F$, $\sigma$ is a sink of $F$ iff $A\cap J=\{v\}$, and the sinks of $F$ among the other vertices
are unchanged; before the flip $\sigma$ is not a sink and $\sigma'$ is one iff $B\cap
J=\emptyset$. So $F$ keeps exactly one sink iff $[A\cap J=\{v\}]\Leftrightarrow[B\cap
J=\emptyset]$, i.e.\ iff $J'\cap(A\setminus\{v\})=\emptyset\Leftrightarrow J'\cap B=\emptyset$ for
every $J'\subseteq[m]\setminus\{v\}$. Taking $J'=\{w\}$ gives $A\setminus\{v\}=B$, and that
condition makes the equivalence hold for all $J'$. The outmap of a unique sink orientation is
injective because $(s(u)\oplus s(u'))\cap(u\oplus u')\ne\emptyset$ forces $s(u)\ne s(u')$.
(b) $s$ being acyclic, a cycle of $s^{e}$ must use $e$, i.e.\ must contain a directed
$\sigma\to\sigma'$ path of $s^{e}$ avoiding $e$; all other edges agree with $s$.
(c) Each flip changes exactly one edge, so the parity of the number of flips at each edge decides
whether it differs; and the sign changes at each flip by (a), while translation by $z\ne0$ is a
product of $2^{m-1}$ transpositions, an even permutation for $m\ge2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[A drive line moves by single combed flips]\label{dl:drive-flip}
Let $t_0$ be a simple fence of a driven block, with the block nondegenerate on a punctured
neighbourhood of $t_0$ and $e$ the tied edge. Then $s_{\mathfrak B}(t_0^-)$ and
$s_{\mathfrak B}(t_0^+)$ agree off $e$; if they differ, $e$ is combed in both and satisfies
\Cref{dl:flippable}(b) in each. Consequently, for $t<t'$ with $\mathfrak B$ nondegenerate at both,
if every fence in $(t,t')$ is simple then their number is at least
$D\bigl(s_{\mathfrak B}(t),s_{\mathfrak B}(t')\bigr)\ge d\bigl(s_{\mathfrak B}(t),s_{\mathfrak
B}(t')\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The level theorem for the escape shape]\label{dl:escape-level}
Let $G$ be a nondegenerate stopping escape extension. Put $\Delta:=1-AA'>0$ and
$\widehat D:=(A'C_\alpha+C_\beta)/\Delta$, $\widehat e:=(A'q_A+q_B)/\Delta$,
$D_1:=A'R_\alpha+C_\beta$, $e_1:=A'q'_A+q_B$. For an inner strategy $\sigma$ let
$\Phi_\sigma(c,d)$ denote the unique $t\in[0,1]$ with $t=c\cdot y_\sigma(t)+d$, and put
$w_{00}:=\Phi_\sigma(\widehat D,\widehat e)$, $w_{10}:=\Phi_\sigma(D_1,e_1)$,
$w_{01}:=\Phi_\sigma(R_\beta,q'_B)$ and
$\rho(\sigma,t):=(R_\alpha-C_\alpha)\cdot y_\sigma(t)+(q'_A-q_A)-A\,t$. Then the drive equals
$w_{00},w_{10},w_{01},w_{01}$ on the layers $(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)$; the inner part of the
improvement outmap at $(\sigma,L)$ is $s_{\mathfrak B}\bigl(w_L(\sigma)\bigr)(\sigma)$; and the
outer part is given by $P:=[w_{00}<w_{10}]$, $Q:=[w_{00}<w_{01}]$, $R:=[w_{10}<w_{01}]$,
$S:=[\rho(\sigma,w_{01})>0]$ through
$O_{(0,0)}=(P,Q)$, $O_{(1,0)}=(1-P,R)$, $O_{(0,1)}=(S,1-Q)$, $O_{(1,1)}=(1-S,1-R)$.
\Cref{prop:pinned-level} is the case $\widehat D=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No escape extension realises a translate by its $\beta$-coordinate]\label{dl:no-beta-translate}
Let $\varphi$ take the value $0$ somewhere and let $\zeta=(w,\zeta_\alpha,\zeta_\beta)$ have
$\zeta_\beta=1$. Then $B_\varphi(s,z')(\cdot\oplus\zeta)$ is the improvement outmap of no
nondegenerate stopping escape extension with outer pair $(\alpha,\beta)$ --- for any pin, any
readouts and any block. In particular $z=24$ and $z=26$ of \Cref{cor:pinned-no-doubling} are
excluded for the escape shape as well.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $\tilde\varphi(\sigma):=\varphi(\sigma\oplus w)$ and read the outer part of the target at
the layer $L$ off the table of \Cref{thm:blowup} at the layer
$L\oplus(\zeta_\alpha,\zeta_\beta)$. If $(\zeta_\alpha,\zeta_\beta)=(0,1)$ then
$P=[\tilde\varphi=1]$, $Q=1$, $R=[\tilde\varphi=1]$, and at a $\sigma$ with
$\tilde\varphi(\sigma)=0$ this is $(0,1,0)$. If $(\zeta_\alpha,\zeta_\beta)=(1,1)$ then
$P=[\tilde\varphi=0]$, $Q=[\tilde\varphi=1]$, $R=1$, and at the same $\sigma$ this is $(1,0,1)$.
Both are forbidden by \Cref{dl:tournament}, the three bits being the pairwise comparisons of the
three reals $w_{00},w_{01},w_{10}$.
\end{proof}
